The chapter title matters because it makes the test immediate. Your First 12 Weeks says the reader is no longer dealing with theory. That is why Big Change and Multiple Goals, Old Habits, and Victim Thinking matter. The chapter sharpens because real execution has to fight on several fronts at once. Multiple goals can overload the cycle. Old habits pull the reader back toward familiar behavior. Victim thinking turns difficulty into a reason to step out of agency.

The chapter then gives the cycle shape through Your First Four Weeks, Your Second Four Weeks, and Your Last Four Weeks. Each phase is not mechanically identical for everyone. The aim is to read the first cycle accurately enough that resistance becomes something to work through and learn from.
